newsitem.title: UK: Northern's fate in balance as bid deadline looms.
newsitem.headline: Northern's fate in balance as bid deadline looms.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric will find out later on Friday if it has successfully fought off a hostile bid from U.S.-based CE Electric.
The dealine for the 782 million pounds ($1.31 billion) bid is 1300 GMT. The outcome, seen in the market as a close call, should be known by around 1700 GMT.
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy, already holds nearly 30 percent of Northern, bought on the open market, and has declared acceptances bringing its holding to around 34 percent.
It hiked its bid to the current 650 pence per share from an original 630 pence on December 6, saying that it had held back the extra fire power in hopes of securing an agreed bid.
Northern's shares were up 3.5 pence by 0950 GMT at 641 pence.
The bid was cleared by UK authorities on December 13, after concerns that it would meet political obstacles had depressed Northern's share price well below the bid level.
Northern claims the backing of its largest institutional investor, the Prudential, which holds around 11 percent, along with M&G and Foreign & Colonial, which has just over one percent.
The bid is the second hostile takeover that Northern has faced -- it spent 560 million pounds fending off Trafalgar House, now owned by Norway's Kvaerner, last year.

That left it with depleted resources to fight this time, but it has promised a 17 percent hike in its dividend and vowed its gearing will be down to 95 percent by March 1997 compared with previous forecasts of 175 percent.
The north of England based Rec has consistently claimed that the bid undervalued it and called for a higher price.
It said 700 pence per share was indicated in talks before CE Electric launched the offer on October 28, a claim which the Americans have denied, saying that the bid is fair value. ($1=.5982 Pound)
